question: Do printed-paper supervision and binary-label exchange improve the existing corner/boundary model without losing clean-design accuracy?

protocol.model: Same 880466-parameter ProposalNet, same frozen checkpoint at the start of every arm. All parameters trainable; evaluation mode freezes BatchNorm running statistics for small batches.
protocol.sampling: Each update has one original training view drawn from a shuffled cycle of all 408 views and one focus view drawn from shuffled cycles of the 75 printed variants. Plain/phase arms use the corresponding original input for the focus view. Identical schedule in every arm.
protocol.augmentation: Joint batch-wide horizontal/vertical reflections with independent 50% coins. Separate per-item 50% mask-complement coins, used only by phase/combined arms; RGB, targets and validity never change with label exchange. All coins and sample IDs fixed before any arm trains.
protocol.selection: Exactly 128 updates per arm. Retain terminal checkpoints only, plus the untouched baseline. No validation, photo, threshold or checkpoint selection during training.
protocol.evaluation: All 308 existing synthetic evaluation views and all 32 real review rows from the pinned evaluation plan, including the six unresolved crops. Original and exchanged mask inference; .6 boundary/.4 junction thresholds, 3px matching, fixed 9px refinement. Reused evaluation sets, not new generalization holdouts.
protocol.inputValidation: Verify all 75 derived RGB/masks, source hashes, binary masks, unchanged original graph/labels/validity references, actual training splits and exact original-input replay before training.

limitations: Single-seed bounded continuation, not a hyperparameter search or final training recipe.
Printed variants cover 25 procedural geometries; they are not real photograph labels.
Thresholded corner and boundary metrics do not establish legal or improved full template reconstruction.
Model remains offline until whole-pipeline and browser checks justify deployment.
